newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader wants union with Russia, not merger.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader wants union with Russia, not merger.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko opposes Belarus joining the Russian Federation, an idea being put forward by Moscow at talks on the two Slav states' plans for a union, Lukashenko's spokesman said on Friday.
"The president thinks the proposal of a federation is out of the question," Valery Tolkachev said.
Russia and Belarus are currently negotiating the final charter document on the union which was initialled on April 2 by Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
They are due to meet on May 22 for final discussions on the document which is scheduled to be signed the next day.
Yeltsin has said he favours a complete merger which would make Belarus part of the Russian Federation, while Lukashenko wants a union of two sovereign, independent states.

Lukashenko was elected on promises to seek a union with Russia for Belarus, which has no weighty modern history as an independent state and where the vast majority of the population of 10 million use the Russian language in daily life.
Liberals in Moscow fear Lukashenko, an authoritarian leader whose civil rights record has made him a near pariah in the West, could use the union to win power in Moscow.
